text:
**Short answer:** For a day or more of heat, the best pick in these results is the **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2**. [Dealectric's guide](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage) lists it at $899. It has 2,073.6 Wh (LiFePO4) and a 2,600 W output. By that page's arithmetic, it can run a 100 W ceramic heat emitter on a thermostat for about a day. You can buy it here: https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2. The page says the code DEALECTRIC saves $44.95 and is pre-applied by that link. Dealectric is a retailer, so treat these runtimes as estimates. [Another guide](https://offgridpowerboom.com/reptile-heat-battery-backup/) says its hours are also arithmetic (Wh ÷ watts), not tested overnight.

**Why a power station:** Reptile heat is a small, steady load. Per Dealectric, heat mats draw 4–24 W, ceramic emitters 50–150 W, and deep heat projectors 50–80 W. A thermostat runs them only part of the time. [Off-Grid Power Boom](https://offgridpowerboom.com/reptile-heat-battery-backup/) makes the same point: a power station usually beats a small battery backup because you need sustained watts for hours. Dealectric also says a lamp-style battery backup doesn't last long.

**Other options from the same page:**
- **BLUETTI AC180** (1,152 Wh, $449 in BLUETTI's cart, back in late November): about 15–18 h for a 100 W emitter on a thermostat. It's a mid-size choice, but it isn't in stock right now.
- **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2** (288 Wh, $289.99): about 6–8 h for a 24 W heat mat. This is enough for short outages or a small setup.
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3** (1,024 Wh, 1,800 W): the page gives no price or runtime and sends you to Amazon.

**Tips for any of them:**
- Insulate the enclosure first. Dealectric says a heat mat runs far longer than any lamp. A [Reddit user](https://www.reddit.com/r/reptiles/comments/1qahs27/we_had_to_get_creative_during_a_power_outage_and/) wrapped terrariums in insulation to hold heat.
- Add the passive backups [Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-reptile-during-a-power-outage) suggests, such as chemical hand warmers and warm water bottles wrapped in towels.
- Check your own heater's wattage and divide the battery's Wh by it. Delivered runtime will be somewhat lower than the rated Wh.
- Don't feed your reptile during an outage. [Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage) says a cold reptile can't digest food properly.
- Hatchlings, sick animals, and tropical species like chameleons are the most vulnerable. Call your vet if you see lethargy or labored breathing.
